csf_outcome: The organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management
Legal, regulatory and contractual cybersecurity requirements are understood and managed
Risk management objectives are established and agreed by stakeholders
Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established and maintained
Leadership is accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a risk-aware culture
Cybersecurity roles, responsibilities and authorities are established and communicated
Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
Cybersecurity policy is established, communicated and enforced
Cybersecurity policy is reviewed and updated to reflect changes in requirements, threats and technology
Strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction
A supply chain risk management programme is established and agreed
Supply chain security requirements are included in contracts and agreements
Supplier risks are identified, recorded, prioritised and monitored over the relationship
Inventories of hardware managed by the organisation are maintained
Inventories of software, services and systems are maintained
Assets are prioritised based on classification, criticality and business value
Assets are managed throughout their life cycle
Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated and recorded
Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources
Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods and impacts are used to understand inherent risk
Risk responses are chosen, prioritised, planned, tracked and communicated
Improvements are identified from evaluations, audits and reviews
Incident response and other cybersecurity plans are established, communicated and improved

csf_outcome: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored and enforced commensurate with risk
Personnel receive awareness and training so they can perform general tasks securely
Individuals in specialised roles receive role-based awareness and training
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data at rest are protected
The confidentiality, integrity and availability of data in transit are protected
Backups of data are created, protected, maintained and tested
Configuration management practices are established and applied
Software is maintained, replaced and removed commensurate with risk
Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring
Secure software development practices are integrated and their performance is monitored
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorised logical access and usage
Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events
Computing hardware, software, runtime environments and their data are monitored
Potentially adverse events are analysed to better understand associated activities
Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria
The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared
Incident reports are triaged and validated
Analysis is performed to establish what took place during an incident and its root cause
Actions performed during an investigation are recorded and the records' integrity is preserved
Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
Incidents are contained
Incidents are eradicated
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated
The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
Recovery activities and progress in restoring operational capabilities are communicated to stakeholders
